title: Deeper/broader implementation-route and evidence-boundary refresh
mode: Primary-source web review plus local plan/repository-state audit; plan update only
head: de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9
scope: Refresh the open-source DWG/DXF comparator set across codec, structural-retention, application-import, and geometry-semantics routes.
Reconcile current project claims with the existing PAR-07/S8, PAR-20, PAR-138, DXF, and downstream-consumer gates.
Improve comparator admission and implementation readiness without creating duplicate findings, new dependencies, or routine peer-test work.

method.kind: Read-only primary-source web review and local plan audit; research receipt and plan edited
method.limitations: This is a source/documentation comparison, not a run of the peer artifacts. Current issue boards are mutable; no issue report is treated as a local reproduction or normative file-format rule. The worktree already contains broad user changes, which were left untouched; only the plan and this receipt were edited.

sources.observed: The project README separates DXF and DWG reader/writer support by AC version. The current issue board contains distinct whole-file/native rejection, data loss, parser robustness, and legacy-framing reports. Issue #1128 proposes recovery for bare top-level TABLE records but supplies no inspectable producer sample in its body; this remains a compatibility report, not a canonical-format rule.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Version/direction declarations and issue reports guide route selection and local tests only. They do not establish a libdxfrw defect, normative grammar, current released behavior, or independent acceptance.

sources.observed: The class documentation distinguishes stable, unstable, debugging, and unhandled support. Unknown-class persistence is described as limited to same-version rewriting when the full raw unknown-bit blob is retained. The README separately discloses DWG-writer version limitations.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Class maturity and project-level support statements are not per-handle semantic or native-acceptance evidence. Raw same-version replay is not typed or cross-version support.

sources.observed: The project documents ASCII and Binary DXF read/write across a stated set of DXF versions and retention of unfamiliar tags except comments. Its issue board contains route-specific binary-proxy and rendering reports.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Independent DXF syntax/tag-structure evidence only for a pinned route. It is not a DWG reader, native CAD application, or general ACIS B-rep validator.

sources.observed: The documentation describes separate C++ and legacy DXF importers, states that stock FreeCAD cannot read embedded ACIS/SAT blobs, and routes DWG through an external converter followed by DXF import. The same page's generic no-loss DXF statement is broader than its importer-specific entity lists.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Only the exact selected importer/backend and converter route can qualify. A format-level no-loss statement cannot establish that a specific importer consumes every entity or ACIS payload.

sources.observed: The public API inventories include named show/label/hatch switches in addition to the style scalar, color, text-style, linetype, and hatch properties. The inventories establish exposed semantic properties, not DWG bit positions or DXF group-code mapping.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Use as a completeness checklist only. Wire mapping still requires the repository-authoritative ODA specification and/or a pinned producer trace.

sources.observed: Broad compatibility prose advertises DWG/DXF and ACIS among many formats, while the detailed table labels DWG as a DXF fallback and ACIS SAT/SAB read/write as planned/unsupported.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Candidate-screen evidence only; not an admitted independent DWG parser, ACIS route, or geometry-semantic result.

sources.observed: The project describes a pre-alpha, specification-based DWG container/section reader with entity-decoder gaps. It documents consulting ACadSharp algorithm comments for one LZ77 ambiguity, which limits independence for that specific algorithm question.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Potential pinned structural differential for implemented container questions only; not a complete semantic or native reader vote.

localCrosswalk.owner: PAR-07/S8 comparator admission and composed qualification
localCrosswalk.observed: Existing owners already separate version/direction, peer artifact maturity, per-record outcomes, recovery, opaque retention, consumer import, and semantic geometry evidence. The refreshed project sources reinforce that route labels must be bound to an actual entry point and output disposition.
localCrosswalk.disposition: Add a compact comparator-row checklist at the existing composed checkpoint: artifact/revision, build/profile, route, direction, source/target version, exact source identity and ownership, diagnostics, and per-object outcome. Do not add a peer runtime to fast slices.

localCrosswalk.observed: The latest local implementation slice closes generated same-version DICTIONARY hierarchy and raw replay only. The existing plan still requires a property-to-field/raw/unsupported matrix before typed serializer completeness, with DWG-origin wire interpretation and native rendering separate.
localCrosswalk.disposition: Retain this as the next local readiness artifact. Source review shows aggregate style flags and two SectionViewStyle group-290 booleans stored under unnamed members; map each exposed show/label/hatch property independently before calling it typed-complete. Group-71 DXF context, ordered repeated tags, DWG field streams, raw replay, and graph closure are separate columns. No typed support claim follows from broad peer class labels or same-codec output.

localCrosswalk.observed: LibreCAD and LibreCAD_3 are downstream compatibility consumers, not independent codec lineages. FreeCAD's stock DXF route cannot qualify embedded ACIS; carrier retention, AcDs association, modeler parsing, geometry semantics, and native acceptance remain distinct.
localCrosswalk.disposition: Preserve 2D compatibility gates and keep each optional 3D consumer/importer named explicitly. Do not let absence from a consumer supported set count as parser loss, or let raw payload presence count as geometry support.

assessment.planEffect: Makes route identity and per-source-object disposition explicit at the existing composed comparator gate; sharpens PAR-138's readiness matrix with the public style-property inventory and unresolved named-flag mapping; preserves the separation between 2D consumers, DXF structural readers, DWG structural readers, ACIS carrier association, geometry semantics, and native acceptance.
